title: PNG SEQUENCE OVERWRITING!!!
content:
![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202511/395154e240074f28afc22a4afbd79621/images/cd410f9a96d441b8ac1dc345e3bb1104IMG-20251117-WA0003.jpg)Hello I am rendering a camera animation of the garment I made in clo . However instead of png sequence frames , it renders each frame as usual but overwrites the previous png. I am rendering a crucial project and need help asap .

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi, it appears to be a bug (so it cannot be fixed until there's a new patch), please downgrade to the previous patch of CLO to render any time-sensitive projects. You can get it here: https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/395154e240074f28afc22a4afbd79621

Comment 2: HI. We are reaching out and reporting this to our team. Thank you
content_description: This page provides urgent support for resolving issues with CLO 3D garment animation rendering overwriting PNG frames instead of saving a sequence.

title: custom avatar measurement problem
content:
![06c56d178cb84f6a93755a82fa40ec72](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202511/c3a5149027a64c9ca43756b031ccc43f/images/06c56d178cb84f6a93755a82fa40ec72%EC%8A%A4%ED%81%AC%EB%A6%B0%EC%83%B7%202025-11-17%20125622.png)![53868455f8d34a1d9fd898963b991475](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202511/c3a5149027a64c9ca43756b031ccc43f/images/53868455f8d34a1d9fd898963b991475%EC%8A%A4%ED%81%AC%EB%A6%B0%EC%83%B7%202025-11-17%20125630.png)![219625fbf7af4d2c990c154c32f3c58b](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202511/c3a5149027a64c9ca43756b031ccc43f/images/219625fbf7af4d2c990c154c32f3c58b%EC%8A%A4%ED%81%AC%EB%A6%B0%EC%83%B7%202025-11-17%20125626.png)

Guys what the hell. I inputed my friend's measurements into the avatar and it became quasimodo.

I tried changing the pose to no avail, it still looks like ...that  


  
The values I tweaked:  
  
Height  
  
Across shoulder(Curveliniar) <this one is the biggest oof but others still make it weird  
  
Chest circumference  
Thigh circumference  
High hip circumference  
Low hip circumference  
Neck base circumference  
Waist circumference  
  
High hip height  
  
Total rise  
  
Vertical trunk  
  


Any help would be appreciated because holy fuck

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: I've found that it is important to start with a size that is simillar to the size im trying to adjust to, ideally within 4cm + or - of my custom meausurments. Try to see what size is closet to you friends measurments firstThen drop that size on your avatar and open the editorStart with the Total height and which ever measurment is to the left of it (Bust usually) Then work you way down each adjustemnt from top of list to the bottom
content_description: This page is dedicated to troubleshooting and seeking advice on avatar customization issues related to body measurement inputs and pose adjustments.

title: Plt export
content:
Hi CLO Team,  
I have a feature request regarding the PLT / plotter export and multi-size pattern exports in general.  
When I use Arrange (disponi), before the layout is generated, all the sizes appear perfectly stacked on top of each other (as shown in the screenshot).  
But once the layout is created, the software automatically spreads all the sizes apart, creating separated pieces.  
For my workflow, it would be extremely helpful to have an option to export all sizes stacked, exactly as they appear before using Arrange — basically keeping the graded sizes overlapped.  
It would also be very useful to have an option to export a PDF with stacked sizes, not only DXF, since the DXF format often creates compatibility issues with some plotters and external software.  
In short:  
– the ability to export all graded sizes stacked exactly as they appear before using Arrange;  
– an additional PDF export mode with stacked graded sizes.  
This feature would be incredibly helpful for anyone working with full size-range pattern development.  
Thank you for your attention!![24ef7a774a794a41a1f5c266a7cab345](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202511/e060322d4db446f18b39596c61feb6e1/images/24ef7a774a794a41a1f5c266a7cab345IMG_8742.png)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hello, you first need to make marker with desired size and fabric width and then export plt. Do not forget to add seam allowance.
content_description: This page gathers user feedback and feature requests to improve multi-size pattern export options, specifically enabling stacked size exports in both DXF and PDF formats for enhanced workflow efficiency.

title: missing clothing templates
